correctness.rationale: For 1D real periodic Korobov smoothness alpha>1/2, Fourier aliasing Q_p-I=sum_{p|m,m!=0} hat f(m). Choosing all nonnegative Fourier coefficients proportional to omega_nu(m)|m|^{-2alpha} attains both triangle and Cauchy–Schwarz bounds for expected absolute error, giving E^2=2zeta(s)nu^T A nu, s=2alpha, A=diag(u_p(1-u_p))+uu^T, u_p=p^{-s}. Positive definite quadratic inverse gives unique w/W by Sherman–Morrison; K=#primes<=p_min and s>1 imply 1-c u_p>0, so no boundary optimum. w_p increases strictly with p. PNT uniform weighted prime sums produce the sharp nontrivial limiting ratio; single-prime edge case covered. Independent exact rational n=12,s=2 gives nu_7=2/7,nu_11=5/7, ratio 301/247; n=30 probabilities positive and increasing. These finite tests are not PNT proof.
